title: Kerala House: VR walkthrough
oneLiner: Walk through a two-storey Kerala house, its garden and play yard, in VR on a Meta Quest 3 or in any desktop browser.
heroAlt: The Kerala house model: a two-storey house with a tiled roof, timber veranda and balcony, set in a walled garden with a play yard

gallery.alt: Close view of the house in flat colour: carved fascia, shuttered windows, brass-banded pillars and a balcony ring
Grey overview of the whole compound: house, walled garden, play yard and palms outside the wall
Early grey blockout of the house, staircase, paths, trees and fence

blurb: A two-storey Kerala house with a timber veranda, a balcony ring, an outside staircase, a walled garden and a play yard. Walk the gate, the hall and the kitchen, climb to the balcony, or teleport around the grounds.
ctaNote: OPENS IN A NEW TAB · BEST ON META QUEST 3, ALSO WORKS ON DESKTOP
galleryHeading: From grey blockout to walkable house
galleryLede: The house was modelled in Blender, then exported as one small file with flat colours and no textures, so it loads fast even on a headset.
how: Model.
Built in Blender with a script, so the whole house can be rebuilt in one run. About 61,000 triangles, 39 flat-colour materials, 1.2 MB.
Engine.
A-Frame (WebXR), loaded from a fixed version. No app to install: it is a web page.
Walkable by name.
Anything named for walking (floors, steps, stairs, paths) can be stood on or teleported to. Everything else blocks you, so walls, furniture and railings behave.
Smooth stairs.
The floor under you is followed with easing, so climbing the outside stairs to the balcony feels steady.
Reset.
One button clears the model from memory and reloads it, which keeps a long headset session stable.
controls: Space to walk, arrows or WASD to steer, R to reset
status: Checked on desktop: the route from the gate to the hall, kitchen and back door, the stairs up to the balcony, wall and furniture blocking, and reset. Next pass: tuning controller aim, comfort and frame rate on the headset.

title: Human Respiratory System: XR anatomy atlas
oneLiner: Fly through a hologram of the human airway, lungs, heart and diaphragm in VR on a Meta Quest 3 or in any desktop browser.
heroAlt: A cyan hologram of the human body in wire mesh with the airway, both lungs, heart and diaphragm inside, labelled, beside a floating XR control panel
blurb: A life-size hologram of the human respiratory system. Follow a breath from the nose down the trachea into 18 branching paths, scale the body up to 40 times, explode the organs apart, isolate one system at a time and watch cyan air go in and warm air come out on a breath cycle you control.
ctaNote: OPENS IN A NEW TAB · BEST ON META QUEST 3, ALSO WORKS ON DESKTOP

gallery.alt: Exploded X-ray view: the ribcage, heart, vessels and trachea separated from the torso shell, with the labels and the control panel
Lungs isolated: two violet lungs with cyan breath particles moving along the airway, everything else faded to a faint outline
Bronchial tree isolated in X-ray view, showing the branching airways inside the faded body

galleryHeading: Four ways to look at one breath
galleryLede: The same model in different views: exploded, with one system isolated, and through the X-ray preset.
how: Model.
Modelled in Blender: body, ribcage, nose to bronchi, both lungs (3 lobes right, 2 left), heart with great vessels and the diaphragm. About 107,000 triangles, 2.2 MB.
Lighting.

The lighting is baked into the model itself: a cyan key light, a violet rim light and ambient occlusion, written into the vertex colours. The headset draws it unlit, so it looks the same everywhere and runs fast.
Airflow.

The 18 breathing paths (10 into the right lung, 8 into the left) were exported from the bronchial tree. The particles ride them: cyan air in, warm amber air out, on a 12 breaths per minute cycle you can change.
Locomotion.

A museum display, not a world to walk around: you ride a smooth circle round the organ you pick, always facing it. Pick an organ in the menu and you glide to it while everything else goes translucent. Hold either stick to the side to circle it, click a stick to exit, run its function, and finish its two tasks.
Reset.
One button throws the model out of memory and loads it again, which keeps a long headset session stable.
controls: Point at a panel button or a label and pull the trigger. Both hands show a laser
Circle the focused organ at a steady speed, in a perfect circle
Exit the focused organ and return to the whole body (also the EXIT FOCUS button)
A cycles the X-ray view, B changes the circling speed
Dock the panel to you, or leave it fixed in space
X resets the view, Y resets the experience
A and D to circle, W and S closer and further, Q and E lower and raise, 1 to 7 to focus an organ, O to circle hands-free, U for its function, R to reset
status: Checked on desktop: loading, the circling path (constant radius and height, always facing the organ), focus and translucency, the laser click path, explode, isolate, the three view presets, the breath cycle, reset and reload. Not yet felt on the headset: laser visibility, trigger response, circling speed.
